title: In 22 larval zebrafish, brain regions with a longer projectome path from the retina had less reliable dark-flash responses, and real wiring predicted this better than rewired graphs
abstract: Question: in mouse, brain regions farther from the retina in the connectome have less reliable visual responses, but distance-preserving rewired connectomes predict this equally well. Does the rule apply in the larval zebrafish, and does the specific wiring add information? Data: Legare et al. 2025 two-photon whole-brain calcium imaging of 22 larvae (1.23 million neurons, 12 whole-field dark flashes, about 1 volume per second) and the directed 70-region mapZebrain projectome of the same authors, which has a retina source. Method: the plan was frozen before region response values were computed. D_ret is the weighted shortest path from the retina through nine retinal arborization-field regions (step cost -log input share). Neuron reliability R is the split-half correlation of dark-flash responses; region value is the median over fish of per-fish medians. Results: region R decreased with D_ret (Spearman rho -0.66, 63 regions; fish bootstrap -0.70 to -0.61; negative in all 22 fish). Unlike in mouse, 1,000 rewired projectomes that keep each target's input weights within distance deciles gave a weaker relation (mean -0.51; p = 0.019). Euclidean distance from the retinal neuropils alone gave rho -0.74; after control of it, and of swim coupling, brightness and neuron count, D_ret kept partial rho -0.36 while rewired graphs gave about 0 (p = 0.004). The result stayed under a spatial-autocorrelation null, without tectal regions, without entry regions, without any single region, and after swim regression. Limitations: coarse atlas regions; an atlas-average projectome from sparse tracings of other larvae; soma-region versus terminal-region mismatch; one stimulus at 1 Hz with swims and arousal; multi-path drive and plain distance predict R better than D_ret, so we do not claim a shortest-path mechanism; the mouse comparison uses published numbers.
